newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland, Russia's Gazprom sign 25-yr gas contract.
newsitem.headline: Poland, Russia's Gazprom sign 25-yr gas contract.

text.p: Poland and Russia's giant state-owned gas supplier Gazprom signed on Wednesday a 25-year contract for supplies of 250 billion cubic metres of natural gas to Poland.

Under the contract -- signed by Gazprom's president Rem Vyakhirev and the head of Poland's Oil and Gas Mining (PGNiG) Alekwsander Findzinski -- the gas would come from a large pipeline that would link the Siberian peninsula of Yamal and Western Europe through Poland.
The construction of the pipeline started early this year.
"The contract envisages the delivery of 250 billion cubic metres of natural gas to Poland over the next 25 years," Findzinski told reporters just before the signing ceremony.
"It is the biggest contract in the history of Poland's gas industry," he said.
Polish Industry Minister Klemens Scierski said on Tuesday that the first three billion cubic metres of gas would flow to Poland in 1997.
He said the amount would be gradually increased to cover between 29 and 43 percent of Poland's needs in the year 2009, estimated at between 22 and 27 billion cubic metres.
The deal sparked criticism from right wing opposition parties that it would expose Poland's energy sector to political risk in Russia.
